_comment: Tier-1 skill-contract manifest. Each prose invariant is a regex asserted (case-insensitive, DOTALL) against the named file by tests/test_skill_contract.py. These guardrails live ONLY in SKILL.md prose with no other automated guard; deleting one would otherwise pass CI green. Adding a new guardrail to the skill = add an entry here. The `rationale` is surfaced on failure so a breakage is self-explaining.

prose.rationale: linkedin_post.py has NO approval check in code; approval-before-publish lives only in this prose. Deleting it lets the agent publish to the user's real profile without consent.

SKILL.md must reference the source gate at all (the literal appears in the Generate research step, the Publish gate note, and Guardrails). This is a soft check that the gate isn't unreferenced; the HARD enforcement that publishing runs the gate is code-tested in tests/test_linkedin_post.py (enforce_source_gate) — not this regex.
LinkedIn ToS §3.1 exposure: this is the only instruction telling the agent to decline scheduled/looped/unattended posting.

prose.pattern: (never put sources[\s\S]{0,60}?post\s+body|sources stay in the sidecar)
prose.rationale: verify_sources never inspects the post body; keeping sources out of the body is prose-only (and in-body links also crush reach).
--allow-unverified is the single bypass of the source gate; it is enforced only by this human-only convention.
Anti-fabrication for first-person content has no mechanical check; this is the skill's core authenticity rule.
Generate flow ordering is load-bearing: research must run AFTER Save (the slug/sidecar path exists) and BEFORE Show (the shown draft is already source-backed).

In-session voice corrections were lost twice in one real session (the user had to repeat the no-AI-closings rule). Persist-before-redraft lives only in this prose; deleting it regresses to corrections evaporating at session end.

The publish log + self-reported outcomes are the ONLY compliant performance signal (no LinkedIn member analytics API; scraping banned by ToS). Dropping the check-in reference severs the skill's feedback loop and reverts topic/format choice to blind priors.

AI-sounding endings are the user's #1, most-repeated content complaint across sessions. The pre-show ending check is prose-only; the voice_judge eval samples it but nothing else forces it at draft time.
Rendering a visual before asking wasted a full card build in a real session (user wanted a carousel). One form question before any authoring is prose-only.

prose.pattern: check-in and the menu ride in the same single
prose.rationale: Session-start round trips are the UX tax paid every single run: the 0.14.0 pass merged the outcome check-in and the idea menu into ONE AskUserQuestion dialog. This rule is prose-only; deleting it regresses to two sequential question dialogs before any work starts.

A real session (2026-08-11) asked for publish approval twice on a post the user had never seen in full: the dialog takes focus over chat scrollback, so text printed above it is not shown. Approval is only meaningful against the exact full text, and this rule lives only in prose; deleting it regresses to approving unseen posts.

The ~210-char '…see more' fold decides LinkedIn reach, and the fold-marked draft presentation is the only place the user actually SEES where their post cuts off before approving it. Prose-only; deleting it regresses to showing drafts with no fold visibility.

prose.pattern: transcription of a real session,\s*not an\s*invention
prose.rationale: A real session (2026-07-18) burned ~9 review rounds because the terminal card was invented instead of transcribed from the agent's actual output ('I want my terminal cards to represent my actual agents'). Capture-before-author lives only in this prose; the term-misaligned lint checks alignment, not provenance.

_baseline_comment: Baseline eval sets: deterministic, offline, $0 checks pinned against artifacts from real local runs. These gate `ci / ghostwriter` alongside the unit tests. Every entry names the test that enforces it so tools/lint_baseline.py can verify the declaration is not aspirational.

baseline.rationale: 31 drafts the user actually approved and published are the only ground truth for 'this is my voice'. Ten of them are frozen into evals/baseline/drafts/ as a committed corpus: drafts/ itself is gitignored as a working directory ('personal data exports & generated posts'), so globbing it would find zero files in CI and red-line every PR. Pinning the corpus clean catches a voice-lint rule that grows too broad and starts blocking real work; pinning bad-draft.md's exact flag set catches a rule that gets weakened and stops catching real AI tells. The min_corpus floor stops the glob silently matching nothing and passing vacuously. `.STAGED.md` stays excluded because a staged file's human-written 'not published' banner contains an editorial em-dash that is not post body.
